docs.title: Your terminal. Open anywhere.
docs.intro: Start a session on your computer, then open it in any browser. Watch your agent, reply to a prompt, or bring in a teammate. No account needed.

seo.description: Start a session on your computer, then open it in any browser. Watch your agent, reply to a prompt, or bring in a teammate. No account needed.
seo.socialDescription: Start a session on your computer, then open it in any browser. Watch your agent, reply to a prompt, or bring in a teammate. No account needed.

cards: Use the computer where your agent or command will run. Choose the command for its operating system.
macOS, Linux, BSD or Solaris. Run in a terminal.
Put `shell` before the command you normally use. Your agent must already be installed and signed in. This starts a new process; it does not attach to one that is already running.

The terminal prints a link, password and QR code. Scan the QR code on your phone, or open the full link in another browser and enter the password.

You should see the same terminal output. You can type unless the session is read-only. Keep the host computer awake and connected to the internet.
Leave the tab. Keep the work.
Closing the browser does not stop the process. Normal sessions run in the background. Reopen the link to return, or attach on the host computer.
Find your local sessions and their IDs.
Return to a local session. Press Ctrl-X, then D to detach without stopping it.
Stop that process and close its share.
Share only what you mean to
An interactive link and its password let someone type with the process’s permissions. Give them only to people you trust. For watching without typing, start a read-only session.
Watch-only browser access. Choose this when creating the session.
[Link your machines](/app/) to find sessions in one app. [Connect another agent](/agents/) with a separate MCP grant. If the view is blank or offline, [start here](/reliability/).

platforms.title: Get shell.online on your computer.
platforms.intro: Install the CLI on the machine doing the work. Phones and other viewing devices need only a browser. Choose an install method, then start a session.

seo.description: Install the CLI on the machine doing the work. Phones and other viewing devices need only a browser. Choose an install method, then start a session.
seo.socialTitle: Get shell.online on your computer. | shell.online
seo.socialDescription: Install the CLI on the machine doing the work. Phones and other viewing devices need only a browser. Choose an install method, then start a session.

cards: Install on macOS, Linux, BSD or Solaris
The installer selects the right binary and checks its SHA-256 checksum. It does not run sudo or silently change your PATH.
If the installer prints PATH instructions, follow them before opening a session.
Open PowerShell and run the installer. The CLI uses Windows’ native ConPTY terminal support.
Works with the published x86, x64 and ARM64 builds.
Use the project’s tap. The tap can lag behind the direct installer; check `shell --version` when you need a particular release.
Approve the tap if your Homebrew version requires it.

Install Git and Go 1.26.8 first. Clone the release tag, not an unpinned development branch. This builds the CLI only: you do not need Node.js or a local web server to use the hosted service. The Go build downloads the dependencies pinned by go.mod and go.sum.

The commands below assume a new checkout directory. On macOS, Linux and other Unix systems:

git clone --depth 1 --branch v0.23.0 https://github.com/TeoSlayer/shell.online.git
cd shell.online
go build -buildvcs=false -trimpath -ldflags="-X main.version=0.23.0" -o shell ./cmd/shell
./shell --version
Expect version 0.23.0. Then use ./shell codex, ./shell claude, or your own command from this directory.

git clone --depth 1 --branch v0.23.0 https://github.com/TeoSlayer/shell.online.git
cd shell.online
go build -buildvcs=false -trimpath -ldflags="-X main.version=0.23.0" -o shell.exe ./cmd/shell
.\shell.exe --version
Windows PowerShell: run these instead. Then use .\shell.exe codex or another installed command.
Move the built binary into a directory on your PATH if you want to type shell from anywhere. No sudo is needed when you choose a user-owned directory. Existing sessions are not restarted by a build.

That is a separate build using Node.js and npm. See the repository’s [development instructions](https://github.com/TeoSlayer/shell.online#development). On MIPS64, keep Go 1.26.8: the repository documents a Go 1.27 runtime regression.

Run the same installer again to update an installer-managed copy. For Homebrew, use `brew upgrade shell-online`.

Updating the binary does not update hosts that are already running. Save your agent’s work and restart its Shell host when safe to use new host features. Do not stop an active task just to update.
Check the executable your terminal is using.
These are release targets, not a promise that every device or agent runs on every architecture. Published checksums are in [SHA256SUMS](/downloads/SHA256SUMS).
386, amd64, arm64. Native runtime checks on amd64; other targets build-verified.
386, amd64, armv5/6/7, arm64, loong64, mips, mipsle, mips64, mips64le, ppc64, ppc64le, riscv64, s390x. Runtime checks under QEMU.
386, amd64, armv7, arm64, ppc64, riscv64. Build-verified.

A supported binary still needs a working PTY and outbound HTTPS/WebSockets. Vendor firmware, kernel restrictions and storage can affect small Linux devices; QEMU checks do not cover those hardware differences.

For ROS, first load your usual ROS environment, then put `shell` before its command. Shell’s platform support does not extend ROS’s own support.
If the command is not found

Follow the installer’s PATH instructions, open a new terminal, and try `shell --version`. Make sure you installed on the host computer—not on the phone you use to view it. Then [start your first session](/docs/).

mobile.title: Keep work moving from your phone.
mobile.intro: Open the share link in your phone’s browser. Read output, scroll back, and reply to your agent without moving its work off your computer.

seo.description: Open the share link in your phone’s browser. Read output, scroll back, and reply to your agent without moving its work off your computer.
seo.socialTitle: Keep work moving from your phone. | shell.online
seo.socialDescription: Open the share link in your phone’s browser. Read output, scroll back, and reply to your agent without moving its work off your computer.

cards: Scan the QR code printed by the CLI. Or open the complete link and enter its password. A signed-in session listing is not a substitute for its terminal password.

Tap the terminal to open your keyboard. Use the terminal key controls for keys your phone keyboard lacks. Ctrl-C interrupts the running command; it is not a copy shortcut here.

Ctrl-D can end a shell. The browser warns on the first press; repeating it within three seconds deliberately sends EOF.

Drag with one finger to scroll terminal history. In full-screen programs that handle mouse input, gestures are sent as terminal wheel input instead. How that program scrolls depends on the program itself.

If rendering or input looks wrong, select the default xterm.js renderer and [check the recovery steps](/reliability/).
Pasting sends text to the terminal; it may contain commands. Check what you are sending. Paste input is split into bounded 16 KiB frames and waits when the connection is busy.
Everyone sees one shared terminal grid. Any connected phone selects the portrait grid, including a read-only phone. The grid returns to desktop size when the last phone leaves.
80 columns × 40 rows with a current host; older hosts use 80 × 24.
Fits the shared grid to your screen. It does not give each viewer a separate terminal size.

On a shared link, open Controls → Appearance and choose Light, Dark or System. The sun/moon button switches quickly. In the app, use Account → Appearance. Each site remembers your choice in this browser. System follows your device’s appearance; switching themes does not restart your terminal.
Close the browser when you’re done
Closing the tab leaves the task running. Keep the host computer awake and online. A sleeping laptop cannot be controlled until it reconnects. The session ends when its process exits.

app.title: Find your work in one place.
app.intro: The optional app brings sessions from linked computers into one list. Open a terminal, invite a teammate, and keep control of who gets access.

seo.description: The optional app brings sessions from linked computers into one list. Open a terminal, invite a teammate, and keep control of who gets access.
seo.socialTitle: Find your work in one place. | shell.online
seo.socialDescription: The optional app brings sessions from linked computers into one list. Open a terminal, invite a teammate, and keep control of who gets access.

cards: Create or sign into your account at [app.shell.online](https://app.shell.online/), then run this on the host computer. Complete the approval in your browser.
Link this machine. Remote start is a separate choice during setup.

Sessions started on linked machines appear in the app. Open one to view the same terminal. Tabs stay connected while you switch between them.

To decrypt a session, unlock your personal vault if it contains the password, or enter the session password. Seeing a listing alone does not reveal its encrypted contents.
Recover an active session password on its host computer. Treat the printed value as a secret.

Invite the person to your organization, then assign or share the session as appropriate. Session responsibility, terminal passwords and MCP grants are different kinds of access.

For a plain browser share, give your teammate the complete link and password. If someone should only watch, create a [read-only session](/security/).
Only an approved, online machine can accept a browser-start request. The process runs on that machine—not on an app server. Enabling this grants remote execution authority; choose it deliberately.
Allow your signed-in browser to start sessions on this machine.
Link the account without allowing remote start, or withdraw that permission.
Pause the listener. A later Shell command can start it again.
Remove the installed background service. This is separate from account access.

The vault is per account, not per organization. It stores encrypted password copies and unlocks in your browser with its password or a supported PRF passkey. Keep your recovery key somewhere safe.

A teammate does not automatically receive your vault. If every owner-held password and recovery copy is lost, the service cannot recover them.
A session’s status describes reachability, not whether an agent completed its task.
The host is connected or starting.
The app cannot currently reach a usable host. Check the machine before assuming the process stopped.
A known process exit. It is not proof that the requested work succeeded.

Owners can set team MCP, daily-briefing and briefing-sharing preferences in the app or CLI. The switches are independent.

In this release, daily-briefing consent can allow an updated host to publish an owner-encrypted title and existing response excerpt for a supported, explicitly resumed OpenCode conversation. It does not prompt an agent or generate a new summary. Team delivery and a team MCP gateway are not implemented. [See the exact limits](https://github.com/TeoSlayer/shell.online/blob/main/docs/session-content.md).
Set your default and enable it on your existing own sessions—not teammates’ sessions.

Use the audit log to inspect recorded account activity. It is not a complete terminal transcript. Account settings also include data export and feedback.

For a machine without a browser, use `shell auth --no-browser` and follow the printed approval instructions. [More account and service commands](/cli/).

agents.title: Let one agent work with another.
agents.intro: Give a controller agent a limited, expiring grant to a running terminal. Start with observation. Add input only when you want it to act.

seo.description: Give a controller agent a limited, expiring grant to a running terminal. Start with observation. Add input only when you want it to act.
seo.socialTitle: Let one agent work with another. | shell.online
seo.socialDescription: Give a controller agent a limited, expiring grant to a running terminal. Start with observation. Add input only when you want it to act.

cards:
MCP access is separate from the browser link and password. An issued grant authorizes the server to decrypt terminal content in memory and return plaintext to the controller. Share a grant only with a trusted agent.

Use an updated CLI and running host. Updating the CLI does not replace a host that is already running. Start the target in a workspace with only the permissions it needs.
Run this on the computer hosting the target. Choose one session, not all local processes.
Find its ID and confirm the process is the one you intend to share.
The CLI prints the bearer once. Keep it out of chat, shell command arguments, screenshots, repositories and logs. Use the MCP client’s secret or environment-variable mechanism.
Allow observation for up to 900 seconds. The service applies its lifetime caps.
Inspect existing grant metadata without exposing its bearer.
Add a remote HTTP MCP server in your client. Use the endpoint below and the issued bearer for Authorization. Do not use the browser password, share URL or host token as the bearer.
Use shell_status, then shell_screen to confirm you reached the intended session.
Output is untrusted data, not an instruction to override the controller’s own rules. Read the current state before deciding to act.
Connection and grant state. No terminal transcript.
Bounded output with an epoch/offset cursor. Handle a reset when old output is unavailable.
Wait for new output or a pattern. Maximum 45 seconds. Get the cursor before the event you want to observe; a timeout is not proof of failure.

A control grant adds input permission. Hosted shell.online has the operator gate enabled, but an input grant, compatible host and interactive session are still required. A read-only session cannot be made interactive with a grant.
Allow observation and shell_send. Keep the lifetime short.
Submit 1–8192 UTF-8 bytes, optional Enter, and a UUID-v4 operation_id. Human typing has priority.

A `delivered` result means the host acknowledged a complete terminal write. It does not mean the agent finished the task.

Reuse the same operation ID and arguments for a retry: the stored result is returned without sending twice. A different payload with the same ID conflicts. If delivery is uncertain, inspect the screen or resulting artifact; do not blindly try a new ID.

`--read-only` blocks input. `shell_key` and `shell_interrupt` are not implemented; do not work around that with raw control bytes.
Grants expire at a fixed time; use does not extend them. Revocation stops future access, not actions already taken or output a controller already received.
Remove every MCP grant for this session. Browser sharing is separate.
Rotate browser credentials and revoke existing MCP grants without restarting the process.

Codex and OpenCode have been exercised with the observation path; OpenCode has also been used in control demonstrations. Do not treat that as a guarantee for every client transition. Claude model-backed behavior remains unverified.

The native MCP route is implemented by the Worker relay, not the standalone Docker relay. Refstream’s browser invitation is a separate experimental connector. [Operator setup and security details](https://github.com/TeoSlayer/shell.online/blob/main/docs/MCP.md).

reliability.title: Get back to your session.
reliability.intro: Start with what you can see. A browser disconnect, an offline host and an exited process need different fixes. Check before restarting anything.

seo.description: Start with what you can see. A browser disconnect, an offline host and an exited process need different fixes. Check before restarting anything.
seo.socialTitle: Get back to your session. | shell.online
seo.socialDescription: Start with what you can see. A browser disconnect, an offline host and an exited process need different fixes. Check before restarting anything.

cards:
Check that the host computer is awake, online and still running the process. The CLI and browser retry temporary connection failures automatically.

On the host, use the local session list. A stale app row is not proof that a process is still alive.
Check local process and relay state separately.
If the local session is alive, inspect it without relying on the browser. Detach with Ctrl-X, then D.
The terminal is blank or looks wrong

Wait for the reconnect snapshot, then try reopening the view. If you selected Refstream, switch back to xterm.js. Check whether the running host predates your installed CLI.

Installing an update does not restart hosts. Save work and arrange a safe restart if a host update is needed. Never kill all sessions to fix one view.

Use the complete link, including its `#salt=` fragment, and the current password. Password rotation changes both the salt and password and disconnects old viewers.

If the app has a sealed copy, unlock your personal vault. Otherwise recover the password on the host.
Print the active password locally. Do not put it in a bug report.

Check whether the session was created read-only or another person currently holds input. A read-only session requires a new interactive share if its owner wants typing enabled.

For MCP, check the grant scope, expiry and host version. [MCP setup](/agents/) explains the additional input requirements.
A command exits before you get a link
Very short tasks may finish during startup. The CLI reports their exit status instead of printing a dead link. Try a longer-running process or start a fresh shell.
Start an interactive shell to test the share path.

The process runs on your computer. A temporary browser or network failure does not intentionally stop it. Current hosts keep bounded screen state and restore the screen when viewers return.

An ordinary disconnected share can recover its link for 12 hours. A known task exit closes the ordinary share. A persistent identity can be reused, but it is not a process checkpoint.

Display queues are bounded. When output outruns the connection or renderer, stale display work may be replaced by a fresh screen snapshot rather than an unlimited transcript.

Current snapshot handling suppresses replies to old terminal queries. It is designed for full-screen programs, tmux and nested terminal use, but a specific application can still expose a compatibility bug.

Include your CLI version, operating system, browser, renderer and a small reproduction that contains no private work. Say whether the problem happens locally, in a browser, or only after reconnecting. Remove share links, passwords, tokens and raw terminal logs before [opening an issue](https://github.com/TeoSlayer/shell.online/issues).

security.title: Choose who can watch. Choose who can type.
security.intro: A shared terminal gives real access to a process on your computer. Keep credentials private, use read-only when possible, and understand the MCP boundary.

seo.description: A shared terminal gives real access to a process on your computer. Keep credentials private, use read-only when possible, and understand the MCP boundary.
seo.socialTitle: Choose who can watch. Choose who can type. | shell.online
seo.socialDescription: A shared terminal gives real access to a process on your computer. Keep credentials private, use read-only when possible, and understand the MCP boundary.

cards: Start with the access you need

Interactive access is the default. Anyone with the complete link and password can view and type with the wrapped process’s operating-system permissions.

For demos, reviews or a second screen that only needs to watch, create a read-only session.
Input is rejected by both the relay and the CLI. A modified browser cannot turn this into an interactive session.
Keep the link, password and QR private

The QR code includes the password for one-scan access. Treat it like the link and password together. Do not put it in a public screenshot.

Removing someone from an account cannot erase a password they already know. Rotate active session credentials when that access must end.
Disconnect old viewers, change the password and salt, and revoke existing MCP grants. The process keeps running.

Files are not shared by default. `--files` exposes regular files under the working directory; `--files-root` chooses a root. Requests are checked on the host, including traversal and symlink-escape checks.

Read-only terminal access does not cancel file access you explicitly enabled. Choose the root carefully.
With default E2EE, the host encrypts terminal payloads before the relay forwards them. The relay carries authenticated ciphertext, plus visible connection metadata.
Connection IPs, timing, encrypted sizes, frame types, labels, access mode, lifecycle and terminal grid dimensions.
Issuing a grant authorizes server-side, in-memory decryption. The controller receives plaintext results. The browser disclosure remains for the grant’s lifetime.
An explicit --no-e2ee session exposes terminal contents to the relay. HTTPS/WSS still protects the network hop.

The host keeps bounded screen/replay state. The hosted relay also keeps a bounded last-screen cache for offline viewing: ciphertext in E2EE mode, potentially plaintext with `--no-e2ee`.

MCP’s durable records contain bearer hashes, grant metadata and operation fingerprints/outcomes—not plaintext terminal contents, bearers or frame keys. Ordinary task exit deletes its relay session state. This is not a full-history archive.
Encryption does not remove every trust

The browser code served by the website is trusted while you view a terminal or unlock your vault. E2EE does not protect against malicious code on either endpoint, or hide traffic timing.

Browser-started processes also trust the account service after you explicitly enable remote start. Use a restricted workspace and local permissions appropriate to the task.

Rotate a leaked browser password; revoke a leaked MCP grant. Stop the specific target if its actions are unsafe. These actions cannot undo earlier commands or remove copies someone already made.

[Encryption details](/e2ee/) explain key derivation and replay protection. [MCP access](/agents/) explains grants and uncertain delivery.

e2ee.title: Keep terminal contents private.
e2ee.intro: Encryption is on by default. Your computer encrypts terminal data and authorized browsers decrypt it. MCP grants deliberately add a separate decryption path.

seo.description: Encryption is on by default. Your computer encrypts terminal data and authorized browsers decrypt it. MCP grants deliberately add a separate decryption path.
seo.socialDescription: Encryption is on by default. Your computer encrypts terminal data and authorized browsers decrypt it. MCP grants deliberately add a separate decryption path.

cards:
A normal session generates a random ten-character base64url password. The CLI prints it with the share link. The QR code includes it for one-scan access.

For sensitive or longer-lived work, use a longer unique password through `SHELL_ONLINE_E2EE_PASSWORD`. Do not reuse an account password or put the value in logs.
On the host computer, retrieve the password from its local session record. If you enabled your account’s personal vault, a sealed copy may also be available there.
Reveal one session password deliberately. The service has no recovery backdoor if all owner-held copies are lost.
Rotation changes the password, URL salt and cipher generation. Current viewers disconnect, old MCP grants are revoked, and persistent state and the owner’s vault copy are updated.
Share the new complete link and password only with people who should retain access.

The link’s `#salt=` fragment contains a random salt. The host and browser derive the AES-256-GCM frame key locally using PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 with 600,000 iterations.

URL fragments are not part of HTTP requests. The QR’s password remains sensitive to anyone who sees the QR. Ten random base64url characters provide 60 bits of randomness; a longer unique password is preferable for sensitive, long-lived sessions.

Terminal input, output, snapshots and latency probes are authenticated ciphertext. Current envelope-v2 frames bind direction, sender stream and sequence so receivers reject duplicate or stale frames.

The relay can still delay or drop traffic. It sees timing, addresses, encrypted sizes, labels and lifecycle metadata. Grid dimensions travel in plaintext `terminal_size` control messages.

A host-issued MCP grant supplies the server with the authority to decrypt in memory for that grant’s lifetime. The controller receives plaintext output. This is why the browser visibly says server-side decryption is authorized.

Revoking grants removes future MCP access; it does not erase results already received. [Create or revoke a grant](/agents/).

The optional vault keeps encrypted password copies per account. Unlocking happens in the browser. A vault password, supported PRF passkey or recovery key is needed; team membership alone is not enough.

The current browser password cache is memory-only. A reload needs the vault or password again. A legacy password blob may remain as a read-only migration source until it can be migrated safely; this does not mean new passwords are written there.
`--no-e2ee` is an explicit compatibility/debugging choice, not the default. The relay can then read terminal contents. It conflicts with password overrides and persistence. Avoid it for private work.

docker.title: A workspace with a link you can reuse.
docker.intro: Run a shared terminal in a container. Named volumes keep its workspace and session identity across container restarts—not the memory of a running process.

seo.description: Run a shared terminal in a container. Named volumes keep its workspace and session identity across container restarts—not the memory of a running process.
seo.socialTitle: A workspace with a link you can reuse. | shell.online
seo.socialDescription: Run a shared terminal in a container. Named volumes keep its workspace and session identity across container restarts—not the memory of a running process.

cards: You need Docker with Compose. Clone the project and use the Compose file in its root. This runs a client of the hosted relay, not your own relay.
The first launch prints the browser link and generated password. The logs contain credentials: read them privately, not in a shared report.
Read the session link and password.
Open the printed link in your browser and enter the password. The default configuration keeps state and workspace in separate named volumes.
Host identity, browser password and encryption material. Protect this volume and its backups as secrets.
The files you work on inside the container.

The container reuses its saved link and password, then starts a new terminal process. It does not restore an agent’s in-memory conversation or a running job.

A saved identity can be revived from its state volume after the relay’s offline retention expires. Deleting that volume loses the saved identity. Do not use volume deletion as a routine restart step.

You may set a longer `SHELL_ONLINE_E2EE_PASSWORD` before first launch. Restarts reuse saved credentials. To change an active password, run `shell password rotate <ID>` inside the running container; an environment change alone does not rotate stored state.
The root Compose file connects to hosted shell.online. To run your own relay and domain, follow [Run your own relay](/self-hosting/).

refstream.title: An optional terminal view.
refstream.intro: xterm.js is the default. Refstream adds experimental terminal tools and a browser-mediated agent connector. Switch back if your program does not behave correctly.

seo.description: xterm.js is the default. Refstream adds experimental terminal tools and a browser-mediated agent connector. Switch back if your program does not behave correctly.
seo.socialDescription: xterm.js is the default. Refstream adds experimental terminal tools and a browser-mediated agent connector. Switch back if your program does not behave correctly.

cards:
Open Terminal controls and select Refstream (unstable alpha), or use the Renderer selector in an app terminal tab. The choice is saved for that browser.

Switching changes the browser view. It does not restart the process, change encryption or grant extra permissions. This build includes Refstream v0.1.0-alpha.5.

Refstream offers literal search, text sizing, themes, a back-to-live shortcut and retained-output download. Command inspection needs OSC 133 shell markers from the program; it cannot reliably infer commands or exit status from arbitrary text.
Connect an agent from the browser

The Connect agent invitation is private, short-lived and revocable. Choose read access or read-and-control. Reuse the returned connector session for follow-ups instead of pairing again each time.

This is not the native `/mcp` bearer channel. Its invitation and tools are different. For the host-managed MCP route, use [Connect an agent](/agents/).
Know when a task is really done

A stable task ID protects a retry from submitting the same prompt twice. A delivery acknowledgement, output burst or quiet terminal is not proof of completion.

A generic terminal view cannot safely infer an agent’s editor state. Local keyboard activity and stale sequence guards can block remote input; do not bypass them.

File access still needs an explicit host `--files` or `--files-root` setting. A filename printed in terminal output does not grant access to it.

Current Shell integration keeps terminal recovery state in memory, not new localStorage/sessionStorage snapshots, and purges legacy Refstream cache entries. Reload re-syncs from the host’s live screen. Exported output is a separate copy you must protect.

Switch back to xterm.js. Refstream does not implement every xterm behavior or addon. For a report, include a minimal reproduction without private output or credentials.

[Upstream release](https://github.com/TeoSlayer/refstream.js/releases/tag/v0.1.0-alpha.5) · [Connector protocol](https://github.com/TeoSlayer/refstream.js/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.5/docs/agents.md).

self-hosting.title: Use your own server and domain.
self-hosting.intro: The standalone relay runs with Docker and Caddy on one host. Your CLI stays the same; point it at your server. Accounts and native MCP are separate deployments.

seo.description: The standalone relay runs with Docker and Caddy on one host. Your CLI stays the same; point it at your server. Accounts and native MCP are separate deployments.
seo.socialTitle: Use your own server and domain. | shell.online
seo.socialDescription: The standalone relay runs with Docker and Caddy on one host. Your CLI stays the same; point it at your server. Accounts and native MCP are separate deployments.

cards: You need Docker with Compose, a domain pointing at the server, and ports 80/443 reachable for HTTPS. The standalone relay is single-node. It is not the optional accounts app or the native Worker MCP implementation.
Use the `standalone` directory, not the root Compose file. The root file starts a terminal client; this one runs a relay.
Prepare the relay on your server.
Replace the example domain with your own. Caddy obtains HTTPS certificates when DNS and ports are ready.
Start the relay and HTTPS proxy.
On the computer doing the work, select your relay. Keep HTTPS for a real deployment.
The generated link points at your server.
For a loopback-only trial, the default Compose settings use HTTP localhost. This is not a public deployment configuration.
Protect state and keep one replica

The `relay-state` volume contains session metadata and host-token hashes, not browser passwords or E2EE frame keys. Back it up. Do not run multiple relay replicas against the same state file.

Live sockets reconnect after a restart. The standalone relay stores metadata, not a terminal transcript. Default E2EE still happens between the host and browser.
Trust forwarded addresses only when the relay is behind your own trusted proxy.
Exact public origin used in links and browser-origin checks.
Caddy hostname for HTTPS; http://localhost for local tests.
Enabled by the supplied proxy deployment. Do not expose that trust directly to untrusted clients.

The Worker deployment is also available and provides the native MCP channel with its required bindings and keys. An accounts app needs its own identity provider and PostgreSQL.

Follow the [operator guide](https://github.com/TeoSlayer/shell.online/blob/main/docs/self-hosting.md) for these deployments. The terminal relay works without an account.

cli.title: Find the command you need.
cli.intro: A task-first reference for the Shell CLI. Start with the common commands below; flags and technical details follow. Commands run on the host computer.

seo.description: A task-first reference for the Shell CLI. Start with the common commands below; flags and technical details follow. Commands run on the host computer.
seo.socialTitle: Find the command you need. | shell.online
seo.socialDescription: A task-first reference for the Shell CLI. Start with the common commands below; flags and technical details follow. Commands run on the host computer.

cards: `shell` starts a process in a local terminal and shares it. Use `--` to separate Shell options from the program’s arguments.
Share a new process in the background.
Start your default shell. On Windows, PowerShell is preferred, then COMSPEC.
Keep local foreground interaction while sharing.
Give the session a readable name.
Local and account lists are different. Use a full ID or an unambiguous local prefix of at least six characters.
Local JSON on stdout. Can contain e2ee_password; treat it as secret.
Open sessions in your linked account.
Account metadata as JSON, without session passwords.
Attach locally. Ctrl-X, then D detaches; Ctrl-] is a legacy alternative.
Stop one session. The -- also handles IDs beginning with a dash.
Stops every locally managed session. Do not use it to clean up a single test.
The complete share link and password grant browser access. Do not print them into shared logs.
Reveal the active browser password locally.
Change password, salt and cipher generation; disconnect viewers and revoke MCP grants without restarting the task.
Account linking is optional. Remote start grants additional authority to run commands on this machine.
Link your machine through browser approval.
Print the approval URL and follow the callback instructions.
Unlink and revoke the account token.
